audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 read Trundle while whys[0] says neither side has a combo and both just farm; Level 6 read Trundle while whys[4] says Ornn's R chains burst his sustain cannot heal; 2+ items read Ornn while whys[6] says his resistance-steal reclaims the extended duel.
audit.why: Trundle's level-1 threat is Chomp, a 3.5s 300-range auto reset that saps AD — real chip, not a kill threat, and Ornn is equally passive. At 6 the double-knock-up chain beats a champion whose only escape is his own terrain. Late, Subjugate plus King's Tribute out-sustains a single-target combo.
audit.corrected: Level 1 -> Skill, Level 6 -> Ornn, 2+ items -> Skill, matched full/content pairs with ratings. Chose Skill rather than Trundle at 2+ items to match the packet chart, since the mirror did not settle that row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 said only 'Trundle's ultimate changes the math'. No ult cooldowns anywhere, and the page treated Ornn as holding the ultimate advantage.
audit.why: Restating the mirror's finding from Ornn's side: Subjugate is 120/100/80 against Call of the Forge God's 140/120/100 — Trundle's ultimate is back twenty seconds sooner at every rank. That inverts the usual 'wait out his cooldown' advice and makes Ornn's R the one that must be spent well.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and breakdown.cooldowns now carry both numbers and the conclusion.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says 'Watch for his E pillar blocking your E-Q wall slam' and wants.foe[1] says Trundle wants to 'Drop his E pillar to block your E-Q wall combo'. That is backwards. Also the packet defect is real: no Trundle ability was named anywhere, and Chomp was called a 'drain'.
audit.why: Searing Charge knocks up on terrain collision, and Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain — so a pillar dropped near Ornn hands him the wall he normally has to build himself with Volcanic Rupture. The mirror audit flagged this exact inversion as its biggest correction. Chomp saps attack damage; it does not heal him. His sustain is King's Tribute off dying units, amplified by Frozen Domain's increased healing.
audit.corrected: report[5].t now states Pillar of Ice as usable terrain; wants.foe[1] rewritten so it no longer teaches the wrong lesson; Chomp named with its 3.5s auto-reset behaviour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was generic, and the page told the player to stack resistances against a champion who steals them.
audit.why: All three flagged missing interactions apply. Frozen Domain increases his healing from all sources, so Grievous Wounds has to exist before contesting his zone. Subjugate steals a percentage of health, armour and MR, doubled over 4 seconds — and Living Forge gives Ornn extra resistances from every source, so that percentage pays more off Ornn than off any other champion. Chomp is also an auto-attack reset, meaning the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
audit.corrected: report[8] names Frozen Domain and sets the timing; dontsFull[1].d and phases[6].why state the Living Forge interaction with Subjugate.
